prompt: Your savings follow $s = 15 + 5w$: you start with $\$15$ and add $\$5$ each week. How many dollars do you have after $6$ weeks?
hint: You begin with some money and add the same amount every week. Find how much was added, then include the start.

hints.text: You begin with some money and add the same amount every week. Find how much was added, then include the start.
Put $w = 6$ into the formula to get $s = 15 + 5 \times 6$. Work out the weekly savings first.
$5 \times 6 = 30$ and $15 + 30 = 45$, so you have $45$ dollars after $6$ weeks.

explanation: Substitute $w = 6$ into the savings formula because six weeks have passed: $s = 15 + 5 \times 6$.
Multiply first to find the money added over six weeks: $5 \times 6 = 30$ dollars.
Add the money you started with: $15 + 30 = 45$, so you have $45$ dollars.

alternativeExplanations.title: On the graph
steps: The savings line starts at $(0, 15)$ and rises $5$ for every $1$ week across.
Six steps of rise $5$ lift you $30$ above the start: $15 + 30 = 45$.
